title: 100 valentines for myself - flower deck and magic rituals deck, only for me
body:
I no longer want to do what I'm told - I will do projects only for me, if I want to. And so, I will buy myself 100 valentines…little heart boxes - Satin, that I can allow velvet to drape into. And if I want to spend six weeks designing, detail by detail, how to print angels on little pillows, then I can do that. And then I will have 100 valentines for myself…and I will keep them.
Perhaps I will make the flower deck, and the magic rituals deck, but only for me - only because I want 500 copies of it. And if they do not sell, I will stow them in boxes - I will keep them, and perhaps I will give them out.

title: PWC handbook - 499 copies as excuse to make one for myself
body: I've got my PWC handbook, which is an excuse for writing what I was forced to observe - the printing - the 499 other copies was an excuse so that I could make it myself - just exactly as I wanted - to look like a passport (so no one could notice (accidental undercover))

title: Reels series ideas: learning to be mean, metaphor machine, set theory, zooming in
body:
Reels I wanted to make:
#1 "I learned to be mean": I felt I had to share gummy bears with Spencer, I only had 5 cause my mom was a health nut. Then…that one day I told Rebecca that her shrug was ugly…I taught myself to be mean, and I've had to be mean ever since.
#2: the metaphor machine
#3: set theory - how we judge art
#4 "zooming in" about abstraction ex. gummy #1 - #2 was some of the essential characteristics, but ends up looking weird cause there's nothing connecting them.

title: Book of dreams idea - right in between reality and fantasy
body: Last night I was thinking to make a book of dreams (cause I found a lot of dreams on scraps of paper in my files) cause that would be the right in between of reality and fantasy…basically just nonsense and who cares about other people's dreams - I couldn't start with "I dreamt" and let people figure it out or not.

title: Tiktok/reels about obsession leading to art-making process
body: I thought I could make a tiktok/reels series where I quickly explain, in a series of white on black screens about obsession, and how that leads into the "art-making process" ("could it be…that this is the same…etc.")

title: Dewey decimal system for ideas - recipe box for concepts
body:
New Idea
Dewey decimal system for ideas. And on the Memory Library one - find a way to "tag" it on the front - + the name….this one: maybe: "Abstract" (idea), and then "recipe" - how to do it.
Also kinda like a recipe box.

title: Luxury items for a Shopify store - useless things, trinkets, building block sets
body:
DIRECTIVE: MAKING LUXURY ITEMS FOR MY NEW SHOPIFY STORE (you know - the one that I already had)
1. GET the blocks - paint them different colors - I can mix them with paint! They could come in one of those wooden cartons - white and mint green label on the top, surrounded by raw wood. Could be a sticker…anyway…other luxury items. Could make like 2-3 or 10, depending on the item, so that IF someone buys it, I actually have one. And I COULD call it "useless things" or "trinket."
Block ideas: bruise blocks - ten blocks, and each is different/various ugly discolored bruises. None are the same. These don't fit together in any particular way.

title: Become a Real Person kit - upscale version with ritual and blocks
body:
I want to make an upscale "Become a Real Person" kit with a printed tea towel and something like the spoon salt shaker - so extra, and includes a ritual attached to it. And then some blocks that can be played with.
A small black plate with handles for no reason. And another one could have a pocket - standalone with a paint brush. Someone says: "put the pocket in the paint brush!" and there's only one way how to do it - you can't do it - but you feel pressured to do it.
"Watch out for the moon: It is too big to carry! (…it might fall on you)"
"I don't have the tools to build a sand castle today."

title: Hinge - a game where the connection is the story itself
body: A parallel game that is maybe more aligned with my original intention called "hinge" in which you basically find the venn diagram with your stories. If you heard a story, and then you could use one of the cards in your hand to tell a new story with the connection. No idea how hard that would be and you could just play them on top of the pile, so - sort of like uno, in that the connection - the hinge - is the story itself. Theoretically, could write 2 words to describe the story and add it as a card. And also everyone would get like 1-2 wild cards per round or per game - that would encourage them to think of their own hinges.

title: Sticker journaling prompts - cut out a sticker when you don't know what to think about
body: I gave myself the assignment to design a game that I can play that keeps me busy and is light exercise for my mind - a walk around the block in its repetitiveness. Elegant solutions so far: XI - draw a card, write down memories. Draw another card. Add a (5 minute) time limit? 2) I have a sheet of stickers and I can't think of what to think about so I'm thinking I could keep the pair of bird scissors in my "purse" and cut out a sticker when I don't quite know what to think about and insert it into my journal, and use that as a journaling prompt.

title: Become a Real Person passport books - set theory, game theory, instrumentalism
body: A passport book called: "become a real person" or "how to…: "set theory" (pink with gold accent. "game theory" (orange) "instrumentalism" (white - all repurposed terms) ANIMANIMALISM, "Art as science; science as art" And lastly: how much could I fit in one book? Table of contents - "the metaphor machine, internal consistency (not set theory), making up a game for yourself, paradoxes…basically, the framework I wanted to explain to J in the museum but he didn't listen… gold, 28 pages - could I do it? A lovely little challenge - to make concise, succinct - the information - to represent it in a way that a non-creative smart person would be able to read.

title: The stamp book and bingo - an advent calendar for collecting patterns
body: Here's another idea: combine the STAMP book and Bingo ideas somehow ex. have envelopes in a stamp book, and whenever you collect an example of that diagram ex - something that is on a pedestal that should not be or competing patterns - you put a little (special) notecard in it (the envelope). And, in fact - if I wanted to work harder not smarter, I could make specialized notecards for each bingo thing - question: how to make it look like bingo. Answer - hang it like this: with cloth pockets - advent calendar

title: Bingo card advent calendar birdhouse - a pattern collector with silver things thrown at it
body: A bingo card => advent calendar => bird house, with matchbox pattern collectors in/for each space - I could throw tiny silver things, like beans or darts at each space, when I think of an example of the concept.

title: Kits with no use - the progression of figuring it out, then making things that really have no use
body: I walked into 4-5 stores on montana - there's a 1-2 block stretch where there's all sorts of trinkets that I don't need. It was so tranquil in that one store, lots of space, light music, and I got the idea of making kits with no use - the progression being - "oh! I don't know what this is:" it's funny for a second, until, and then, you figure it out. But then I could make things that really have no use - that just have that rustic feel - I was especially inspired by a cast-iron gadget, whose purpose I could not understand.

title: Reverse scale - an exercise in acceptance that measures nothing, it is a ritual
body: a reverse scale - where you have to accept the paradoxes/competing patterns ("it is an exercise in acceptance" - also - it measures nothing - it is an act - a ritual. (AND it looks nice - it comes in a wooden box. You collect some sort of pattern, to which there is evidence on both sides, and then place pebbles accordingly, and readjust whenever you do. Some material could work mechanically. I think wood and metal (cast iron).

title: Pattern collector to thome to pebbles - each memory recollected until the pattern stores
body: step one: pattern collector, step two: pebbles on the thome. In the updated version, each event has a varied aesthetic, making it possible to connect and remember individual events, hence, step two, in which the pebbles are lain on the thome, and each memory is recollected until the pattern begins to store.

title: Sticks in a porcelain dish - you collect them like ideas for an essay, then tie them with a bow
body: sticks that are ideally not picked from the ground - the bark is removed, and then they are wood-stained (varnished), so they are prepared, but they are natural, and there is the right degree of variation and finish. They go in another one of those boats (made of porcelain). You collect them - like ideas for an essay, over the course of a few days (probably at most a week), in the dish, and then tie them up with a white bow string (old) and there is some effort, and it is like collecting ideas for an essay.

title: Competing patterns sticker set - special ghost, duplicitous envelope, ambiguous events, two sides of the same coin
body: specifically picking the stickers: special ghost is my friend, the duplicitous envelope, ambiguous events, competing patterns, two sides of the same coin, state 1, hidden mechanism, state 2 - you'd never imagine that there was something in between them that was this. For example: when Chris gave the key - enabling us to be stranded. It seemed as though it was a natural stage to stage transmission. But there was this hidden mechanism.

title: Clearing Things Up - a TV show where I explain the reason, but they're looking at me cause it wasn't staged
body: "Clearing things up" - a tv show I invented when M and D were confused about why mommy says Doris differently. The background would blur, and I would explain the reason, but they'd be looking at me, cause it wasn't staged. (for autism, by autism).

title: Bandaids in a large egg - pick one every morning, maintaining the black outline by painting between them
body: I wanted to make the bandaids, and put them in a "large size egg" and keep it at the front of my house and pick one every morning - the brilliant part was to maintain the black outline by painting (black) between the bandaids.

title: Assembly line castles - developing a technique for making many small things
body: I ended up making 3 castles - that's a lot! I even developed a technique for doing so - roll out the clay, cut it approximate - forgot to measure - score it together, cut the turrets, cut the window. Making a bunch of small things was the goal - assembly line style.

title: Interactive art store - autopros displayed so you can take one out and play with it, then put it back
body: somewhat interactive art store - someone manning the counter where the autopros are displayed and you can take one out and play with it (clay and wood?), and then put it back (and it goes in a "cookie-phane" bag). They can just be displayed like that, and have more behind them. Patterns I've collected, and memories I've had throughout the day.

title: Daily significant moments on cards - 5-12 things that stood out to you
body: Making the little card thingies with all the little pieces of your day, like the salad thing - a thing that was significant - that stood out to you - apart from all the other things that happened to you during the day. If you just had all your days, and like 8-12 things that happened to you on any one particular day (maybe 5 if you're being realistic) - and then you could just go back and look at all your days that you had.

title: Exercises for the teaching kit - filling containers, science telephone, set theory into sculptures
body:
I could write down all the exercises - things that I know need to be there. And then, I could fill in the explanations of why they are there (and these could be in the right order, too?)
Filling containers with things. "What's the procedure - science telephone." Set theory - a few stages, as it turns into sculptures/figures. Making up your own game. All the games I thought of - pokemon action figures (trying to figure out what things have in common - so far this has been done with hoonies - I could show them with hoonies, and they could do it with something else (ideally they do it with moment)). Once they have established the structure/procedure - comparing things, trying to see what they have in common, then they can apply it to anything.

title: Kit ideas - clay ring with curtain, doll heads for collecting friends, hoonie box
body:
Had this kind of like idea for a kit. Could have hoonie new ones inside of it. And then it could have a black like clay thing in it. But it must be dripping black. And it should probably just have like a doll head with long ringlets so the body would be the black thing - and just painted black.
Also: make like a clay ring and then attach a curtain to it with a thread or wire - wire rings. Improvise sewing. And you could also make the heads for collecting friends if they are hard - make them out of…can Robinson make plastic parts or find someone that does.

title: Solitaire - train of thought as game
body: Solitaire - the new name for game two. SOLITAIRE. But the cards would be different, as they would all refer to something... Train of thought as [game]. Grabbing it as it goes.

title: Love Potion #9 - checkerboard design with gold, green, pink and maroon
body:
I've wanted to buy those snug fitting cylinders for a cheap price for some time now. I would draw a checkerboard of green, pink and maroon with gold, or cherry red line outlining it at the top. And leaves, drawn like two nice small figures pulling down.
Love Potion #9. Silver. And, with sticks in a hexagon around. Things get caught in it.
To design the love potion: I would like to paint, in gouache - a medium brown, slightly dark, like milky coffee (in a touch of texture, like coarse mustard). There would be a separation point, a breath of edge, where all the "squares" stop to be beset by the label, but the label is an indent, not an exdent.

title: Ritual, Instrument, Apparatus, Thingamajig - the curated collection
body:
Ritual, instrument, apparatus, thingamajig. The curated collection.
Matches - inside the matchbox is a "ring... is a room." Instrument - ideally, polished metal, with some kind of bristles threaded through the holes. Thingamajig - easy to produce. Each one has a string that belongs to it. Each one has an angel that belongs to it.

title: Instruments of Abstraction - my bible, the chosen pages distilled
body:
This morning I realized I always have the weight of the passport book that I carry here in my hand to put (keep) that in my bag - replacing a special book with one that I make myself (travel kit in bag) and I wanted to replace the words with Instruments of Abstraction.
MY BIBLE. Inside: the chosen pages or the chosen pages distilled.

title: Messing up chess - the board becomes a memory of the game you had
body: Chess board - as part of the tik tok series - and part of it is that you have to "mess" up the board, every time you wanna move a space. I thought: ok, but how would you maintain alternating colors, but then I thought: no - maybe fine - not to - and then the end result is the board - completely mismatched - a little memory of the game you had and the progress you took - the journey - as if you could trace the steps.

title: Photo memory blocks - a picture of your memory wrapped around different sized wood
body: It could just be a black and white photo printed on a graph, wrapped around differently sized wood. Instead of it being a gift you give someone - it's a picture of your memory, where your family lives or your many partners. The sizes could be variable. The other thing is to make it into a block set, to explain to your child how you have many partners, or how you would love more than one child. Is it a coincidence that a heart sort of looks like a house (home is where the heart is).

title: Stamp idea - wherever you go, stamp it - BINGO cards for places
body:
I could stamp the last few pages - "I wrote in my journal, drew in my journal, watched at beach, at pier - etc - wherever you go - paper." I could just have the stamp myself, on site then to the business, or they pre-stamp them. "Replica watercolor guide." And punch out BINGO CARDS. Can I be a simplified version - with just ONE eye, and a monocle?
STAMP: PRIMO PASSO, CAFE LUXE, I WATCHED PEOPLE AT:

title: Gold bubble wand necklace - temporarily blow up an idea like a soap bubble then it pops
body: I imagined selling or wearing a gold bubble wand necklace to represent how you temporarily blow up an idea or belief so you create a soap bubble, as it gets bigger and bigger, and you use it for something, and then it pops. Like a bible, the one symbol saying confidence and knowledge.

title: Solitaire - the new name for game two - but the cards would all refer to something
body:
Solitaire - the new name for game two.
SOLITAIRE.
But the cards would be different, as they would all refer to something...

title: Completist gumball machine - put in a quarter, get nothing or your money back
body: My completist gumball idea where you put in a quarter, and you get either: nothing, 25 cents, 50 cents, 75 cents, or 100 cents. So, you could win back your money, or and then some, or nothing (and feel stupid. I think you'd feel stupid).

title: Memory library - wooden rack where each slot is a concept and each card is a memory
body: Memory library. A wooden rack where each slot is a concept and each card is a memory. You file your memories by what they taught you, not when they happened. The rack itself becomes a map of your mind - you can see which concepts have lots of memories and which ones are thin.

title: EZ-Book Design insight - simplifying decisions into bite-sized chunks
body:
I watched EZ-Book Design, and said to myself, that the people in the comments didn't know why it was appealing…he simplifies the process of making decisions into bite-sized chunks (tricks you into thinking there weren't a million more decisions - as though determinist - the way he chose was the only way - to watch is to believe that making decisions is easy - the paradox - it's about making decisions - he both explores indecisiveness, and takes it away.)
I know exactly how that design process feels - automation + artificial - get an idea - automaton (do it - in a way that can be undone - then: intuitive mind: "do I like it"). The hidden mechanism of turning it on and off.

title: Bad Ideas Box - all bad ideas, and that's why I don't want to do them
body: I GUESS I COULD PUT IT IN MY BAD IDEAS BOX…THAT is a good idea - one I should actually do. And it solves a problem - like majorly - cause then I can just say they are all bad ideas, and so that's why I won't/don't want to do them. For example - the mango thing - is that a particularly good idea? Idk. Certainly the sugar waiting game is not exactly a good idea. And: none of the words sounded quite right except: BAD IDEA.

title: Meta games - people need to learn pattern collecting and set theory before they can play
body: META GAMES - people need to learn what pattern collecting is, AND set theory, and people as paradoxes before they can play any of the other games - other games ex. collecting specific patterns. Because, for example: last night: ex. I thought of another set - going out (includes receipts to look like cards).

title: Chaining thoughts - one thought isn't interesting, you need two to prove a pattern
body: What I was thinking about was chaining - how, a thought by itself isn't interesting, but if you wire two together - then it's interesting. Which is crazy. But like - if I have a thought that I think is interesting, then I can't write it down, till I think of a similar thought, and then I have a chain, and then I have a pattern - and then I've proved it twice.

title: Broken games make me feel fine - it's broken in a way the world is broken
body: The measuring spoons that I got excited about last night - like the aspect where you make it not work. I don't like it working - things like that stress me out. Broken games make me feel fine - it's broken in a way the world is broken. Otherwise I feel I have to win.

title: He loves me not coin - a bad idea because the game is a ritual
body:
Impression of people coming up with ideas:
instead of [flower game], why not have: [coin] - "he loves me, he loves me not"
lol → see, cause this is a bad idea - and yes, it's more efficient. But it's not what the game is about. The game is a ritual. Because people don't understand the underlying reasons why people do stuff.

title: Set theory + kit theory - apply the SET mindset to know what rules to use
body:
Set theory + kit theory - what do they not have in common. Opposite + set theory - apply the SET mindset so you can know what rules to use when creating the thing.
Ok - procedure - define all the concepts - make them like pattern blocks, where each is a different color and/or shape - hex code - candyland - then put them together into constellations.

title: Setting things up for later - edge yourself - add 3 things to short term memory
body: Here's another common ToT - setting things up for later ex. rather than thinking about this now, lemme "edge myself" - add 3 things to my short term memory so it's more fun to think of it.

title: See something interesting - what kernel did you find in it - compare it to something else
body: If you see…something that interests you…try to make more examples, so that - when you see them all together - you can find out "what you were looking at…what your head was doing."

title: Avenue of Thought - each repeating pattern is an autopro that can be stopped
body: AoT (avenue of thought): Each thought that fits into the same pattern - like a little constellation shape is an autopro and can (should?) be stopped with an artificial pro.

title: You refine what you're doing to match the specific block - sugar packets stacking widthwise
body: You get the blocks, or the sugar packets or the 3D pea rounds with lace and the first thing you do is maybe try various configurations that make sense to you. As the castles topple, the sugar "cubes" fall down, you gradually refine what you're doing to be more in line with the specific "block" you're using until you are stacking the sugar packets widthwise instead of trying to make them stand up.

title: A booklet of complete nonsense that makes complete sense - brain turned inside out
body: I think the thing that got me excited was remembering myself playing dolls when I was little, and the idea of someone asking what are you teaching them, and I would pull out this whole giant booklet that looked like complete nonsense, and the further you read, the more you got into it, and finally, when you finished it, you would know for sure it was nonsense, but it would make complete sense to you now.

title: Thought modifier - an internal meme with a caliper on the end
body: Another thing that I think is going to be on the test is a thought modifier which can come in the form of an internal meme, or a trailing sentiment and it has a caliper and a small tool on the end - long - nothing on the end, but doubled and bent - caliper keeps it still - and to see into the mechanism - medium wood block.

title: Two interpretations of matches - coincidences or things in common
body: There's two interpretations of "matches" (as in: match book or book of matches), and they are: 1. coincidences or 2. things that match - two people wearing the same color red outfit, or a pattern: having the same thought process multiple times.

title: Crossword puzzle layout - linearity solved by laying cards on top of each other
body: The frustration of a lack of linearity because once something got in my mind, it was still in my mind was actually solved by the problem that become the crossword puzzle layout and the new rules - laying cards on top of each other to make them more precious and fleeting. Looking like a chess board with a white vs. black border.

title: Recreational journaling - only the parts where I don't talk about how I feel about people
body: To think of a procedure - to go through all my notebooks and find where I don't talk about how I feel about people - nothing "practical" in the sense that journaling is to make your emotions feel better. Only recreational journaling. :)

title: The criteria for saying something - a checklist you can change with therapy
body: Earlier today I was thinking about the criteria for saying something. I think of it like this (and if it follows all of the check marks, you can sit (or think it)) And you can maybe change the check marks - temporarily - with different people and permanently on purpose - with therapy.

title: Serotonin jump game - going through thoughts to see what chemical they produce
body: I guess this is the game that I am playing - trying to find a thought to make the serotonin jump, and the rules are that you just go through all your thoughts and wait to see what chemical it will produce, and once you're done, then you can stop thinking the thought.

title: The relaxation ritual - frumps in a cup to end thought cycles
body: A relaxation I played the other day was gradually adding solid objects to a cup of tea/coffee - dark objects, frumpy - mechanism - each frump represents one thought, and you put it in the cup to end the cycle - to finish thinking about it.

title: Uno but in their heads - you can play any card
body: Made up a game - uno but in their heads - you can play any card - she played "flower" and I pollinated her flower cause we'd been talking about how flowers are created for bees to see.

title: Memory fragments with expiration dates - a different kind of deadline
body: As an example of a game I could play, I will write down fragments of memories, that will become null and void in about 2-3 days (the time it takes to forget things) - a different kind of deadline. And before that time is up, I will assign myself to go back and look at them and decide whether I would like to keep them, or let them go.

title: Recording diary entries as audiobooks - a project of no use to anyone but me
body: Yesterday I decided, against all that is holy because it is useful, to record some of my diary entries as audio books, so I could listen to them. Perhaps as I fall asleep, and perhaps while I work in the garage. I finally have a (time-consuming) project that is of no use to anyone but me.

title: Instrumental heuristics - helpful metaphor becomes a structure for the book
body: for Robert - instrumental heuristics - a possible structure for the book - a description/a feel into - metaphor for the concept - with retrograde motion or not, and then - all the (progressive) ways you can apply it - "helpful metaphor → instrumental heuristic".

title: Mind feelings trying to place feeling feelings - little things with tiny names and labels
body: mind feelings are trying to place feeling feelings - they look like little things w/ tiny names and labels - all the concepts that are stored in my brain, that I pretend I can call on when I need them.

title: The Play concept - a fully formed thought complete with beginning and end
body: I think, if I started speaking, I could, I would, come out, with a fully formed thought, complete with thought beginning and thought end - and I'd always researched it - in my mind.

title: Collecting counter-intuitives as ritual - like a sack of oranges over your shoulder
body: I thought collecting the lil' counter-intuitives was a ritual to make me feel like I have control. But it's also like collecting a sack of oranges, heaving it over your shoulder, and also like: the bingo card, large, hung on the wall, like a twister game, like a chess board, where the pebbles are the pieces.

title: Backwards recall - your mind generates things to write when you're trying to remember
body: The goal is memory recall - if I'm trying to think of something to write down, (pen, poised above paper - I can't think of it - the right thing to write) - then my mind automatically starts coming up with "oh, you could write this."

title: Saving things on your inner wrist - peace of mind and Buddha's burgers
body: I saved three things on my inner wrist in the shower - and the middle one was peace of mind, the bottom one was a certain amount of time, and the last (top) was buddha's burgers, where I watched my mind start thinking of all sorts of examples and noted that as a worthy mechanism to be taken advantage of in the future.

title: Second arrow shield - writing things down to prevent madness
body: I put things together when I write - I make metaphors that only I understand. And I'm worried that later, I won't remember them. So I wrote it down as a second arrow shield. To prevent madness. My daily reminder: things have meaning.

title: Topological approach to pattern collection - the medium sieve of my new loafers
body: On an outing with my mother, I found some rare breed of small pinecones which looked evil. I decided to use these for the curated nature collection, and in the kit, I knew I needed to have some pebbles. Flat ones might be nice - something between a pebble and a penny.

title: Essential characteristics as substitute - add a roof to anything and it's a house in the room of the mind
body: like the army men, it doesn't have to have legs, it just has to look like it could. So you can substitute the essential characteristics for the thing itself - you can add a roof to anything and it will be a house (in the room of the mind).

title: Hidden mechanism of preparing puzzles for other people - making it hard for them to know what you're saying
body: what does belong in the same book is: the hidden mechanism/intermediate stage of: preparing puzzles for other people (and making it hard for them to know what you are saying) - it's very important to only use big words if you have to.

title: Games like Clue are narrow - I believe in Colonel Mustard, pretendland with a real and imaginary mat
body: Games like "clue" are narrow - the dumpster thing - redesign - cause I believe in the characters. I believe in Colonel Mustard! Pretendland (with a real and imaginary mat).

title: Journaling for continuity - to make sure at any given moment I agree with myself
body: I didn't wanna tell him that all I can do is affirm, and that, a large part of my journaling is for continuity - to make sure that, at any given moment, I agree with myself (maintain consistency).

title: Deck of cards outline concept - revolutionary cause not using properties at all, just a flat surface
body: I was looking at a deck of cards on that shelf in the hall. I borrowed one aspect - an outline - just the basic outline - revolutionary, cause not using the properties at all - just a flat surface, with nice rounded corners.

title: Sugar packets into clay - extracting one purpose at the detriment of another
body: People playing with the sugar packets when they are bored waiting for their food. Now the sugar packets are made out of clay (and so is the dish, as it was before) (MAKE THIS). The sugar packets are converted into just this game.

title: Decision tree then apply a program - initialize shoe tying program
body: Decision tree - consider all the options at the fork, but then, choose one, and ignore all the other options for the time being. In the meantime, "apply a program" - a preset program. Tying your shoes is one, brushing your teeth is another.

title: Non-linear story - all the information organized thematically instead of linearly
body: The idea that, if you read a book, you read it linearly, and by the end you reorganize all the information a bunch of times. Instead, what if you had it all already organized and then you could just see exactly what it looked like at the end.

title: The clock without numbers - falling asleep procedure with blanket and tweezers
body: The clock without the numbers - when you're trying to fall asleep - take the shape, then you want to just put a blanket over it to muffle the sound, trying to turn my brain off so I can fall asleep. Then you can take tweezers out and pull the things out from under the blanket and brush their fur off and pat them on the head; send them out to play.

title: Velope - an envelope with the letter on the outside
body: LOVE LETTER. Velope - "an envelope with the letter on the outside."

title: Is a sculpture not a solution
body: Is a sculpture not a solution.

title: Shaking the plastic maze - deconstraction's main action is waiting
body: Just the metaphor of shaking one of those plastic mazes with a little ball inside - trying to find the right narrative that will make everything nice and right. It's the process of deconstraction - its main action is waiting - letting yourself wait.

title: Different size nets for different size thoughts - try all the spoons
body: Different size nets for different size thoughts. So I have to try all the spoons, to see which one works for any particular thought. Try it out, to see if it is the right size, and eventually it will be.

title: Examplification - think of the example then find the phenomenon
body: Made up a new word: examplification which means - when you think of an example, and then you try to think of the phenomenon that describes it.

title: Story rules - DO tell one story, DON'T tell a phenomenon that occurred lots of times
body: DO: tell a story with a beginning, a middle, and an end. DON'T: tell a fact. DO: talk about a specific event. DON'T: talk about a phenomenon that occurred lots of times. DO: tell one story. DON'T: tell lots of stories.

title: Talmud - iterative process - print it in the middle of the page
body: TALMUD - iterative process - just one! I researched how the talmud is laid out. Proud I knew what I wanted to research and stayed researching it. Print it in the middle of the page.

title: Self-awareness hall pass - allows you to never go to school again
body: He doesn't know about my self-awareness hall pass that allows you to never go to school again - those codes Pandora's Box that made it actually fun to play - cheat codes.

title: Blowing a bubble and catching it in a net - collecting patterns because you can't get into someone's universe
body: Like blowing a bubble, and catching it in a net, given an inelegant net purpose, then I had to remember it and draw it here. Being in it, not of it - collecting patterns, because you don't want to, or can't get into the universe of the other person.

title: A thought got caught as you were pulling it out of the basket
body: A thought got caught as you were pulling it out of the basket. "No! Wait!" The thought floating down into the sea.

title: Three wheels that spin independently with retro drag - to see what they have in common
body: Three wheels that spin independently - with a little "retro drag" on each - to help when you see what they have in common.

title: Saving things as portraits or snapshots or constellations - Sarah as three moments
body: I think saving things in portraits, or snapshots, or constellations - for example, if Sarah would be saved as three specific moments. This is the way things are saved in our head - of the space in between stuff. It helps you remember the idea, like a mnemonic device, but it's used as a diagram.

title: The kit is a ceremony for opening - it teaches you how to use things by making you discover them
body: The kit is a ceremony for opening. It teaches you how to use things by making you discover them. You pull back the layers and each one is a lesson. The wrapping is part of the product - not packaging, but pedagogy.

title: The game is: how few pieces do you need to still recognize the thing
body: The game is: how few pieces do you need to still recognize the thing. Like a caricature - three lines and you know it's Nixon. That's the essential characteristics. The game of abstraction is always subtraction - what can I remove and still have it be the thing.

title: VOMIT method and the DREGS - writing the most important stuff first
body: One reason I liked the VOMIT method is that he called attention that there is an "invisible procedure" - I start by documenting what I've been doing recently. I guess I would include a new category called the DREGS which is dependent on a time constraint - I should write the most important stuff first.

title: Moving in a line - start with the main concept and get more and more granular
body: Moving in a line (linear) start with the main concept - general broad idea (which is a map for where you want to go) and get more and more granular. Main concept -> shell concept -> shell concept

title: Leave a thread to pull on instead of blueprinting - start with the imaging
body: The idea I had is: really starting with the imaging. That would mean, to follow the progression - to start with an abstract - to draw the shape of it first, and instrumentally, maybe being honest about which parts I don't actually know - leave that part conspicuously blank.

title: The thome - a theme that is also a home for ideas to live in
body: The thome. A theme that is also a home for ideas to live in. Not a category - categories are dead. A thome is alive - ideas move in and out, they have neighbors, they influence each other. The thome grows as you add to it.

title: Think of stickers as words - they're both abstractions, they both point at things
body: Think of stickers as words. They're both abstractions. They both point at things. When I put a sticker on a page, it's like putting a word in a sentence - it means something in context that it didn't mean alone.

title: Data points connected by straight lines - don't have to write the whole essay
body: The point of my equation thing is that I don't have to write the whole essay - just the data points, and they can be connected in the imagination as long as there's a straight line between them.

title: Filters are temporary beliefs you hold while sorting - instrumentalism for categories
body: Filters are temporary beliefs you hold while sorting. You pretend something is true long enough to organize by it, then you drop it. This is instrumentalism for categories - you don't have to believe the categories are real, you just have to use them.
